title: Normalized cube blocks
statement:
For natural numbers $n$ and $m$ and a Boolean vector $x\in\{0,1\}^{nm}$, define $z\in\bbr^n$ by
\[
z_i=\frac{1}{\sqrt m}\sum_{j=1}^m \varepsilon\bigl(x_{(i,j)}\bigr),\qquad i=1,\ldots,n,
\]
where $\varepsilon$ is the sign encoding of a Boolean value and the coordinate $(i,j)$ is identified with its position in the length-$nm$ vector.
hypotheses_covered: $x$ is a Boolean vector of length $nm$
caveat: The supplied context does not define the sign encoding or specify the coordinate ordering induced by the product equivalence, so these conventions cannot be stated exactly.
